passages.title: Tidewater Offshore Wind Outlook 2026
passages.text: Installed offshore wind capacity in the fictional Tidewater region reached 4.2 GW at the end of 2025. FICE projects 9.8 GW by 2030 if the Marlow Bank auction clears on schedule. Grid connection queues remain the main constraint; the average wait for a connection offer rose from 14 to 22 months.

passages.title: Tidewater Offshore Wind Outlook 2026
passages.text: Supply-chain bottlenecks for export cables and installation vessels are the largest schedule risk. A two-year slip at Marlow Bank would cut the 2030 projection to 7.6 GW.

passages.title: Tidewater Offshore Wind Outlook 2026
passages.text: The levelised cost of electricity for fixed-bottom projects fell to 61 EUR/MWh in the synthetic 2025 auction round, down from 74 EUR/MWh in 2023. Floating projects remain above 120 EUR/MWh. FICE attributes the decline to larger turbines (15 MW class) and lower financing costs.

passages.title: Analysis note: heat pump adoption in Brightwater
passages.text: Heat pump installations in the fictional municipality of Brightwater doubled between 2023 and 2025, from 3,100 to 6,300 units per year. The subsidy scheme covering 40 percent of installation costs explains most of the increase; installer capacity is now the binding constraint.

passages.title: Battery storage in Kestrel Valley
passages.text: Deployed capacity. Grid batteries in the fictional Kestrel Valley reached 850 MWh in 2025.

passages.title: Ferrow hydrogen pilot results
passages.text: The fictional Ferrow steelworks ran a 20 MW electrolyser pilot through 2025. It produced 2,600 tonnes of hydrogen at an average cost of 5.8 EUR per kilogram.

passages.title: Grid tariff reform in Hollin
passages.text: The fictional Hollin Energy Regulator introduced time-of-use network tariffs in January 2026. Peak charges (17:00 to 20:00) rose to 9.4 cents per kWh, while off-peak charges fell to 2.1 cents per kWh.
